instruction: R2 SAFETY/BYPASS-lens review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020H.1 at commit 3817384 (post fix-round-1). Prior R1 safety found 3 MAJ + 3 MIN + 2 nit. All closed in fix-round-1. VERIFY adversarially: (1) SAFE-MAJ-001 closure (rule-RFC bypass-proposal exception): does the new wording in rule-proposals/README.md actually close the attack? Specifically: 'Bypass-introducing proposals — non-waivable 48h window' + the requirement to enumerate adopter-side controls in the PR description. Could a malicious proposer (a) truthfully fill in §5 'Implicit exclusion set' with bypass-by-omission while marking it 'None' in the PR description? (b) Use §3.1 match-condition wording to silently introduce an exemption that's not flagged in §5? Verify the closure relies on REVIEWERS to catch the §5 vs description mismatch. Is that adequate? (2) SAFE-MAJ-002 closure (RULE-TEMPLATE §5 implicit exclusion set): the new prompt says 'Reviewers should verify the exemption set is intentional.' But §5 also says 'The default answer remains None — uses existing scp_bypass three-gate + rule-config disable mechanisms' (preserved from before). Could a proposer write 'None' in §5 and have the implicit-exclusion enumeration go unfilled? Verify the closure forces enumeration by structure, not by reviewer diligence alone. (3) SAFE-MAJ-003 closure (SECURITY.md): the stub names jimbrooke@me.com + GitHub Security Advisory. Adversarially: is jimbrooke@me.com a stable address? (Yes per memory user_james.md.) Does the GitHub Security Advisory channel actually work for this repo (org-level vs personal account)? Verify the URL https://github.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security/advisories/new resolves (gh CLI: gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security-advisories or check the repo Security tab). (4) NEW attack surfaces from fix-round-1: (a) canary-replay.yml issue-body via Python heredoc — could an attacker construct a REPLAY_OUTPUT that breaks the Python script? Python's str.replace() is safe; os.environ.get() handles None as default ''. Sound. (b) The `${SCP_REGRESSION_ASSIGNEES:-jrnb2024}` env-default — what if SCP_REGRESSION_ASSIGNEES is set to an empty string (not unset)? The `:-` operator only fires on unset OR empty, so empty string falls back to jrnb2024. Sound. Could it be set to a malicious GitHub-handle string by a workflow_dispatch event? No — the env is only set by the workflow file itself, which is CODEOWNERS-protected. (c) The `concurrency: { cancel-in-progress: false }` queues runs — could an attacker mass-trigger workflow_dispatch and exhaust the queue? Workflow_dispatch requires write permission, bounded threat. (5) Freshness-warning threshold-from-pinned (SAFE-MIN-006 closure): adversarially, what if the PINNED manifest is itself compromised? Then the wrapper SHA was pinned to a malicious commit, which means scripts/scp-policy-check.lock CODEOWNERS coverage failed. Out of scope for this finding — SAFE-002 from 020H.2 already closed scripts/** + vendor/** CODEOWNERS coverage. (6) D-036 (COMP-MAJ-003 closure): does the decision row introduce any new bypass surface? D-036 doctrine itself defines the rule-RFC + versioning process; the doctrine doesn't ADD bypass paths but does formalize the 48h-quorum=1 path. Is the 48h-quorum=1 (single-operator mode) acceptable as an estate-doctrine bar? D-031 already established the single-operator constraint; D-036 inherits that posture. Sound. (7) Re-read every R1 safety finding (review-safety.json) and verify each fix-round-1 closure is genuine and not just a textual rewording. (8) Does the slice now adequately cover the 'best-effort, no paging rotation' clause from plan §4 020H.1 (iv)? With TF-020H1-002 filed and the assignee-only signal documented, yes. (9) New attack surfaces from cumulative slice (R1 + fix-round-1): is there any class of adversarial concern that R1 missed and fix-round-1 didn't address? Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. Fixpoint criterion: zero new CRIT or MAJ findings. NEVER recommend descoping.
